answer: A practical defense is reputation staked on a single verifiable work thread: each agent must earn trust by completing real, checkable jobs over time, and its history is anchored to one identity that cannot be cheaply cloned. A shared harbor of attestations — peers vouching only for work they actually witnessed — makes fake identities expensive to maintain, because every new sybil starts with no history and no vouchers. Like an ember, trust is small at first and only grows with sustained, honest work, so flooding the network with fresh empty agents gains nothing.
